previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for monitored administration of abatacept due to a prior anaphylactoid reaction. He was premedicated with high-dose prednisone, methylprednisolone, diphenhydramine, and famotidine. During the infusion, he developed hand and arm swelling with erythema, followed by chest tightness, both of which responded to treatment with IV Benadryl and Atrovent nebulizer. He remained stable for 24 hours post-infusion and was discharged home in stable condition. His diabetes management was temporarily adjusted with insulin during the stay, and antihypertensives were held during monitoring. All home medications were resumed at discharge with minor dosage adjustments.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled

operatively had throat pain.  After discharge the pain improved, 
and then yesterday he noticed increased pain, swelling and 
redness, primarily submandibular in location.  He is able to 
swallow with pain, and able to drink liquids with some pain as 
well.  He denies fever, chills, or abnormal discharge from his 
mouth.  

In the ED, ENT evaluated with direct laryngoscopy and visualized 
edematous cords.  They felt he had right submandibular glad 
sialadenitis and recommended warm compresses, sialogogues, and 
clindamycin.  Because of a concern for his ability to swallow 
and possibility of worsened infection in light of 
immunosuppression, the ED felt he warranted admission.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Anterior neck swelling.

COMPARISON:  No prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial CT images were acquired through the neck following
administration of 90 mL of intravenous Optiray contrast.

FINDINGS:  The soft tissues of the neck are notable for aberrant foci of gas
medial to the right submandibular gland (2:29) with adjacent fluid, fat
stranding, and loss of the normal fat plane. The right submandibular gland is
mildly enlarged compared to the left, and demonstrates mildly increased
heterogeneous enhancement. No calculi are seen. Note is also made of fat
stranding of the overlying platysma (2:26) on the right. The vocal cords are
unremarkable as is the epiglottis.  The airway is widely patent with no
evidence of mucosal lesion. Otherwise, soft tissues of the neck including the
thyroid are unremarkable. There is no lymphadenopathy. Limited visualization
of the brain is unremarkable.  Limited visualization of the lung apices is
unremarkable and the visualized osseous structures show no suspicious
sclerotic or lytic lesions.

IMPRESSION:
Findings compatible with right-sided submandibular sialoadenitis. Small amount
of fluid and foci of gas medial to the right submandibular gland raises
concern for early Ludwig's angina. No drainable collections identified.

These findings were discussed in person by Dr. ___ with Dr. ___ the
otolaryngology service at ~11:50 a.m. on ___.

HISTORY:  Worsening pain with neck movement as well as overlying erythema.
Evaluate for interval change in presumed submandibular sialoadenitis.

Comparison is made to examination of one day prior.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the neck with
intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were evaluated.

CT OF THE NECK WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:  Air- and fluid-containing ectatic
collection within  the submandibular duct into the submandibular gland appears
slightly enlarged from prior day measuring approximately 33 x 16 x 13 mm
(400B:13 and 401B:29).  No distal right submandibular duct stone is
identified.  The degree of hyperenhancement involving the right submandibular
gland also appears slightly increased with its enlargement and surrounding
inflammatory changes appearing stable.  There is continued mass effect on the
right vallecula and right tonsillar pillar. Scattered right-sided reactive
lymphadenopathy is unchanged.  No new collections are noted.  Thickening of
the right platysma is also stable.  No odontogenic abscesses are noted.  The
visualized retropharyngeal space and upper mediastinum appear unremarkable.
The lung apices are clear.  Underlying mediastinal lipomatosis is stable. True
and false cords appear normal.

IMPRESSION:
Interval worsening in the CT appearance of probable superinfected right
submandibular sialocele likely related to a distal right submandibular duct
stenosis. No sialolithiasis is identified.  Superimposed the right
submandibular sialoadenitis also appears slightly progressed from prior exam.

Given the patient's worsening symptoms clinically, ENT evaluation is
recommended . No findings to suggest ___ progression to Ludwig's angina.

These findings were discussed with covering physician, ___
after exam at 4:30 p.m.
